description: Create a task. A "schedule" task needs exactly one of dow, cron or every_days. To put a task in a loop, create it with task_type "loop", then call enqueue_task.

cron.description: Cron schedule, 5 fields; only the date fields (day of month, month, weekday) matter: minute and hour are ignored, so write them as "0 0" (e.g. "0 0 * * 1" = Mondays). Alternative to dow and every_days (one schedule system at a time). Do not use "*/N" in the day field for "every N days": it restarts each month; use every_days.

dow.description: Days of the week as a bitmask: Monday=1, Tuesday=2, Wednesday=4, Thursday=8, Friday=16, Saturday=32, Sunday=64. 127 = every day, 31 = weekdays. 0 = none (use with cron or every_days).

end_date.description: Last day it applies, YYYY-MM-DD. null clears it.

every.description: Subtasks: armed every N runs of the parent.

every_days.description: Strict interval: due every N days, counted from start_date (the anchor; defaults to today in the user's time zone). A missed day does not shift the cycle. Schedule tasks/loops only, and instead of dow and cron (send dow 0 / cron null with it). null removes it.

is_active.description: false pauses it without deleting it.

start_date.description: First day it applies, YYYY-MM-DD; with every_days, the first day of the interval. null clears it.

task_missed_behavior.description: Schedule tasks: what happens when a due day passes unchecked. "reschedule" keeps it armed, "drop" skips it automatically (abortions +1).

task_type.description: "schedule": due on its dow, cron or every_days days (exactly one of them). "loop": a member of a loop's queue (then use enqueue_task). "subtask": armed every "every" runs of parent_task_id.

name: create_task
title: Create a task
